request.description: Same as Create Checkout Intent, with the optional insurance fields on a basket item. A payment takes them on this route only (Checkout Form); `direct/payment` and the marketplace intent answer them with 400. The insurance requests take the same item in `context.items`. `insuranceCategory` is the item kind (TICKET, HOTEL, EVENT, DEVICE, ELECTRONICS, VEHICLE, TRAVEL, HOME, HEALTH, PET, MICROMOBILITY, MUSICAL_INSTRUMENT, SHIPMENT, EDUCATION) and is required when `insuranceTypes`, `insuranceValueAmount`, `insuranceContext` or `insuranceData` is sent. `insuranceTypes` narrows the category's insurance types; `insuranceValueAmount` is the insured value of one unit in minor units (default: the unit price); `insuranceEligible: false` turns insurance off for the item. `insuranceContext` prefills the type's fields (the buyer can change them) and carries no personal data; an unknown key is a 400. The personal data the quote needs goes in `insuranceData` (next request). With any insurance field in the basket, item `id`s must be unique. The fields do not reach the payment provider; when insurance is not offered the payment goes on unchanged. `itemType` is PHYSICAL or VIRTUAL.

Same as Create Checkout Intent (Insured Item), plus `insuranceData` on the ticket: what the quote needs that only you know (the insured, the PNR, the ticket number …), so the buyer is not asked for it again. The keys are the root fields of the type's quote body: `policyholder`, `insured` and the type object (`tickets`, `stay`, `device`, `product`, `vehicle`, `trip`, `rental`, `instrument`, `event`, `accident`, `procedure`, `pet`, `residence`, `abroadStay`, `property`, `health`); field names and formats are those of the insurance types reference. A list type object (`tickets`) is ONE object here, for this item, without `basketItemId` (the item `id` is used).

Partial data is allowed: the Checkout Form asks the buyer only for what is missing, and prices the insurance on its own when nothing is; the buyer still ticks the box and the insurer's consent. `insuranceCategory` is required with it; an insurance premium item (`id` `inso_…`) cannot carry it; leave it out instead of sending `{}`. The gateway checks the shape (an object of at most 16 KB as JSON, known roots, `insured` 1–10 objects, the format of each known field, no `null`) and answers `400` with the field path (`basketItems.0.insuranceData.tickets`), never the value. Data the type's schema does not accept does not stop the payment: it is not stored, the buyer is asked for it and `Insurance › List Insurance Products for a Payment` shows why in `insuranceDataIssues`.

It is personal data: it never reaches the payment provider or the payment record, Lunixi stores it encrypted for the insurance quote only and erases it after the payment intent expires. The values here are made up (a passport number of zeros, a sample PNR and ticket number); never put a real person's data into a shared workspace. item.name: Payment Methods
item.description:
Payments with any payment method from the merchant server: Faturana Yansıt (charge to the mobile phone bill), wallets and card.

- `GET /payments/methods` lists the methods open for your account (enabled in your form settings, with a provider connected), in the order set in your form settings: `blockName`, `providerSelection` (`ROUTED` card, `OPTIONAL` `providerCode` may be omitted, `REQUIRED` send `providerCode`), `providerSelectionMode` (the API behaviour: `BUYER` send `providerCode` when more than one provider is connected; `PLATFORM` `providerCode` may be left out and the platform picks a connected provider, 422 `payment.provider.none_eligible` when none can take the payment; in the Checkout Form the buyer always picks the provider), `splitEligible` / `splitBehavior` (split payments), `preauth` support, limits and each provider's `inputFields`. `?paymentMethod=MOBILE_BILLING` lists one method (`{ methods: [] }` when it is not open, 400 `payment.method.unknown` for an unknown code).
- `POST /payments/direct/payment` starts the payment. The body has `paymentMethod` and only the block of that method (`mobileBilling`, `wallet`, `card`); order fields are `buyer`, `billingAddress`, `shippingAddress`, `basketItems`, `paymentChannel`, `paymentGroup`, `description`, `customerId`, `metadata`. **Idempotency-Key** is required. A key outside the DTO is `400` (`forbidNonWhitelisted`).
- When the buyer must act the answer is `202` with `data.action`. The folder stores `data.action.id` in `payment_action_id` (and `paymentId` in `payment_id`). `OTP`: put the code in `payment_otp` and send **Confirm Payment Action**; **Resend Payment Action** sends a new code and stores the new action id. `REDIRECT` (card with `force3D`): open `payment_action_redirect_url` in a browser.
- A wrong code is `422` with `details.attemptsRemaining`; the action stays open. A declined payment is `400`.
- The final result also arrives by webhook (`payment.captured`, `payment.failed` …) with `paymentMethod` and `providerCode`.

**Run order:** List Payment Methods → (List Payment Methods - One Method) → Direct Payment - Faturana Yansıt → (Resend Payment Action) → Confirm Payment Action. The wallet and card requests start new payments and overwrite `payment_id` / `payment_action_id`.

This is the only server-side card charge: `paymentMethod: CARD` with the `card` block (a stored card: `cardUserKey` + `cardToken`), `force3D: true` for 3D Secure. The former direct 2D/3D card endpoints were removed; the Checkout Form card flow (`form/2d|3d`) is unchanged.

item.name: Split Payments
item.description:
One payment funded by several legs: stored cards and, when split payments with other methods are enabled in your form settings, non-card methods (Faturana Yansıt, wallet, promissory note).

- `POST /payments/split`: `totalAmount`, `currency`, `ownerRef` (your customer's card owner key), `orderId`, `callbackUrl` (required when a card leg sets `force3D`) and `legs` (1 to 5). A card leg is `{ cardToken, amount, force3D?, installment?, installmentQuoteToken? }`; a non-card leg is `{ paymentMethod, amount, <block> }` with the same block as `direct/payment` and `providerCode` required (a provider with `splitEligible: true` in **List Payment Methods**). Leg amounts add up to `totalAmount`. **Idempotency-Key** is required.
- The platform sets the order of the legs (credit approval, card holds, reversible charges, the non-reversible charge last) and returns it as `steps`; `pendingStep` is what the payment waits for. While the payment runs the answer is HTTP `400` with the split status (`AWAITING_ACTION`, `AWAITING_3DS` …) as `code` and the split in `data`.
- `pendingStep.step` `ACTION`: the folder stores `pendingStep.paymentId` in `split_leg_payment_id` and `pendingStep.actionId` in `split_leg_action_id`; put the code in `payment_otp` and send **Confirm Split Leg Action**. Then send **Continue Split Payment**: the same body with the same Idempotency-Key (`split:{{split_order_id}}`). No new payment is created; the payment continues where it stopped.
- `GET /payments/split/{id}` returns the legs with amounts, refund state and chargeback mark; `POST /payments/split/{id}/refund` refunds the main payment (card legs first, then the other refundable legs; a non-reversible leg is never refunded).
- Deliver the order on the main payment's webhook (`payment.captured` / `payment.failed` with `settlementMode: SPLIT` and `legs[]`). Leg events reach an endpoint only when its event types include `payment.split.leg_events`.

**Run order:** Create Split Payment - Card and Faturana Yansıt → Confirm Split Leg Action → Continue Split Payment → Get Split Payment → Refund Split Payment. Set a new `split_order_id` for each new split payment.

item.name: Promissory Notes
item.description:
Senetle Ödeme (`paymentMethod: PROMISSORY_NOTE`): promissory notes (or payment orders, by your provider connection settings) issued through the provider's API. There is no buyer action: on success the payment is `CAPTURED` at once (`200`, no `action`). The money does not pass through Lunixi; each note is collected at its due date from the debtor to your own account.

- The `promissoryNote` block carries the debtor and guarantor fields the provider declares in `inputFields` (**Payment Methods → List Payment Methods**). Do not hard-code a provider: read it from that list (`providerCode` may be left out while one provider is connected). Field types: `ADDRESS` (`{ provinceCode, districtCode, neighborhoodCode, line }`, codes from the **Reference** folder), `GROUP` (list of objects, e.g. `guarantors`), `VKN`; a field with `requiredWhen` is sent only when the sibling field has that value (e.g. `companyTitle`, `taxNumber` for `debtorType: CORPORATE`). Name, e-mail, phone and identity number may come from `buyer` (`prefill`).
- The plan is `schedule` (`[{ amount, dueDate }]`: minor units adding up to `amount`, `YYYY-MM-DD` after today in Istanbul, ascending, at most 24 rows) **or** `noteCount` (one of the `noteCount` options, within your connection limits), never both. Currency is `TRY`.
- **Idempotency-Key** is required on `direct/payment`.
- Errors: a malformed schedule (not a list, more than 24 rows, a non-integer amount, a date format, an extra key) is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; plan and field rules are `400 payment.method.block_invalid` with `details.errors[] = { field, reason }` (e.g. `promissoryNote.schedule[1].dueDate` / `not_in_future`; an intent schedule with another pinned method: `not_allowed_for_<METHOD>`), `422 payment.provider.not_available`, `404 payment.promissory_note.not_found`, `503 payment.promissory_note.document_unavailable`.
- Webhooks: `payment.promissory_note.paid`, `.protested`, `.cancelled` (payload `promissoryNote: { serialNumber, sequence, amountMinor, dueDate, status, occurredAt }`); statuses are polled from the provider, so they arrive some time after the due date.

Example values are synthetic. Set `promissory_note_district_code` and `promissory_note_neighborhood_code` from the **Reference** folder and keep the due dates in `promissory_note_due_date_1/2` in the future.

**Run order:** Create Checkout Intent (Promissory Note Schedule) → Direct Payment - Promissory Note (Note Count, Corporate) → Direct Payment - Promissory Note (Schedule) → List Promissory Notes → Download Promissory Notes (PDF) → Cancel Promissory Notes. Each payment overwrites `payment_id`; the list stores the first open note in `promissory_note_serial_number`.

item.description:
Webhook endpoint yönetimi + teslimat operasyonları (DEAD_LETTER, replay).
İmza: `x-lunixi-signature` header'ı virgülle ayrılmış `v2=<hex>` item listesidir — tek şema v2'dir; liste biçimi yalnız secret rotasyonundaki 24h grace penceresi içindir (`v2=<yeni>,v2=<eski>`).

Item'ları timing-safe karşılaştırın; HERHANGİ biri eşleşirse geçerli, `v2=` item yoksa REDDEDİN.
Retry: 12 deneme / ~52h (10s→24h, ±%20 jitter) → DEAD_LETTER; replay bütçeyi sıfırlar.

item.name: Wallet
item.description:
Closed-loop wallet, merchant server-to-server API (`/api/v1/wallet/*`): end users, wallets, transfers, withdrawals, top-ups, payments, QR codes and bulk payouts. One request per route.

**Signing.** Every wallet route is behind `SignatureGuard`: reads included, each request carries the per-request Ed25519 signature (`X-Key-Id`, `X-Date`, `X-Nonce`, `X-Signature`, `Digest` with a body). The collection pre-request script signs every request; nothing to do per request. Unsigned is `401 AUTH_HEADERS_MISSING`. The merchant, its programs and its end users come from the signing key.

**The key needs** the `WALLET_SERVICE` product (403 `PRODUCT_NOT_ENABLED` otherwise) and the permission behind each route (403 `WALLET_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` otherwise):

| Permission | Routes |
|---|---|
| `wallet:*:read` (`wallet:program:read`, `wallet:enduser:read`, `wallet:operation:read`, `wallet:qr:read`, …) | ping, reads, quotes, QR parse |
| `wallet:program:manage` / `wallet:enduser:manage` (set-up: `wallet:program\|enduser\|limit\|fee:manage`) | collection anchor; end users, wallets and accounts, wallet lookup, deposit instructions, freeze |
| `wallet:operation:intervene` | money inside the wallet: W2W, card and agent top-ups, top-up refund, payments |
| `wallet:bank-payout:operate` | IBAN transfers, bank withdrawals, simulated inbound credit (GROWTH plan) |
| `wallet:qr:manage` | create and revoke QR |
| `wallet:bulk:create` | corporate accounts, employee import and offboard, create and reject bulk payouts |
| `wallet:bulk:approve` | submit, approve, process and retry bulk payouts (the approving key must differ from the creating key) |
| `wallet:enduser:kyc-override` | update the KYC level |

Payment request and collect also need a **wallet terminal bound to the signing key**.

**Bodies.** The gateway rejects an unknown body field with 400 (`forbidNonWhitelisted`); the bodies here contain only fields the gateway accepts. **Amounts are minor units as digit strings**: `"12550"` is 125.50 TRY, never a number or a decimal.

**Idempotency-Key.** Required on the routes that create or move something (the request has the header; 1-128 characters after trimming). It is a fresh `{{$guid}}` per send; to test a replay, pin it to a fixed value and send twice.

**Two-step money.** W2W, IBAN transfer and bank withdrawal are initiate + complete; payment is request + approve. The first step answers `operationId` (payment: `requestId`), `integrityHash`, `nonce` and `otpRequired`; the folder stores them in `wallet_operation_id` (payment: `wallet_payment_operation_id`), `wallet_integrity_hash`, `wallet_nonce`, and the second step sends them back. Complete bodies also carry `operationId` equal to the path id. When `otpRequired` is true, add `"otpCode"` to the second step's body.

**Run order.** Programs (fills `wallet_program_id`) → End users (create, chains the end user, wallet and account) → Wallets & accounts → Deposits (the simulated inbound credit funds the account on a test bank integration) → Corporate → Fees → Transfers W2W → Transfers IBAN → Bank withdrawals → Operations → Top-ups → Payments → QR → Bulk payouts → End-user lifecycle (freeze, last). Before running, set `wallet_destination_wallet_no` (another end user's wallet number), `wallet_business_end_user_id` (a BUSINESS end user), `wallet_rail_id`, `wallet_agent_id` and, for collect, `wallet_payment_code`.

Wallet responses never overwrite `payment_id` or `checkout_token`.

item.description:
Insurance sold with your own checkout (`/api/v1/insurance`, product `INSURANCE_SERVICE`): products, quotes, orders, the premium in your Lunixi payment or collected outside Lunixi, policy documents, cancellation, premium refunds, reconciliation and leads for the types sold by request only.

- **API key only.** Every route needs the per-request Ed25519 signature, reads included; the collection signs every gateway request. Unsigned is `401 AUTH_HEADERS_MISSING`; without the `INSURANCE_SERVICE` product `403 PRODUCT_NOT_ENABLED`. The insurer connection is set up in the Lunixi dashboard.
- **The key decides the environment.** A TEST key (`mk_test_…`) works on test insurance orders only.
- **Bodies** carry only the fields the gateway accepts; another top-level field is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Amounts are minor units as JSON integers (`4900` is 49.00 TRY); times are ISO 8601 with a time zone.
- **Idempotency-Key** (`insurance-…-{{$guid}}`, fresh on every send) is on create order, confirm payment, issue policy, cancel, refund premium and submit lead, where it is required, and on bind payment, where it is optional. Pin it to a fixed value to test a replay.
- **Set before running:** `insurance_insured_identity_type`, `insurance_insured_identity_number`, `insurance_insured_birth_date`, `insurance_insured_email`, `insurance_insured_phone`, `insurance_ticket_pnr` and `insurance_ticket_number` (the insured person and the ticket, as your checkout collects them); for a lead also `insurance_vehicle_plate`, `insurance_vehicle_registration_serial` and `insurance_vehicle_registration_number` (the vehicle of the lead; the person is the insured above). The template leaves them empty: never put a real person's data into a shared workspace.
- **Chained variables:** `List Cities` fills `insurance_city_code` when it is empty; a quote sets `insurance_quote_id`, `insurance_terms_version` and `insurance_terms_sha256`; an order sets `insurance_order_id`, `insurance_premium_amount` and `insurance_payment_amount` (ticket + premium); every order answer that has a policy sets `insurance_policy_id`; a lead sets `insurance_lead_id`. Insurance answers never overwrite `payment_id`.

**Premium in Your Lunixi Payment:** quote → order → create the payment with the ticket **and** the premium item (`id` = `orderId`, `VIRTUAL`, `price` = `premiumAmount`; `amount` is the sum) → bind. Open the Checkout Form with `checkout_token` and pay; once the payment is captured the policy is requested on its own.

**Premium Collected Outside Lunixi:** quote → order → you collect the premium → confirm payment → issue policy.

**Leads:** submit lead → list or read it. A lead is a request to the insurer, not a sale: no quote, premium, order or policy.

Results arrive by webhook (subscribe an `INSURANCE_SERVICE` endpoint to `insurance.*`): `insurance.policy.issued`, `insurance.policy.failed`, `insurance.refund.required`, `insurance.policy.document_ready`, `insurance.policy.cancelled`, `insurance.refund.completed`; for a lead `insurance.lead.submitted` (a lead summary: `lead.leadId`, `insuranceType`, `status`, no personal data). Decide on the webhook; `Get Insurance Order` shows the current state. Policy document, cancel and refund work once the policy is issued (`policyStatus: ISSUED`).

An insurer that collects the premium itself (`premiumCollectedBy: PROVIDER`) cannot be completed through this API yet: confirm payment, issue policy and refund premium answer `409` (`collected_by_provider`).

**Insurance data:** a basket item can carry `insuranceData` (the insured, the PNR, the IMEI …; personal data, stored encrypted for the quote only) so the buyer is not asked again: `Payments / Checkout › Create Checkout Intent (Insured Item + insuranceData)` → `List Insurance Products for a Payment` (`prefill`, `providedFields` masked, `quoteReady`, `insuranceDataIssues`) → `Create Insurance Quote (paymentIntentId, merchant data)` with no type fields.

item.description:
Outgoing transfers and currency exchange from connected bank accounts (`/api/v1/bank-connect`, product `BANK_CONNECT`). Available on a connection whose `capabilities` include `OUTGOING_TRANSFER` (transfers) or `FX_EXCHANGE` (exchange).

- **Scope `bank-connect:transfer`** on every route, reads included (`403 API_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` otherwise).
- **IP allowlist required.** A key with this scope must have an IP allowlist (`403 bank_connect.auth.ip_allowlist_required`), and the request must come from a listed IP (`403 bank_connect.auth.ip_not_allowed`). Postman must run on a listed machine.
- **No e-mail code with an API key.** The key's scope, the signature and the source IP approve the request: a transfer or an exchange order is `SUBMITTED` at once and queued for the bank.
- **Idempotency-Key** is required on `Create Transfer` and `Create FX Order` (8–200 printable ASCII). The requests send a fresh `{{$guid}}` per send; pin a value to replay.
- **The key decides the environment.** Sending `environment`, `merchantId` or any other field the route does not take is `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- **Limit:** 20 write requests per minute per API key (transfer, quote, order together); `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`.
- Run the Bank Accounts folder first (it fills `bank_connection_id` and `bank_account_id`). Fill `bank_receiver_iban` / `bank_receiver_name` for a transfer and `bank_fx_source_account_id` / `bank_fx_target_account_id` (two accounts of the same connection in different currencies) for an exchange. The folder stores `bank_transfer_id`, `bank_fx_quote_id` and `bank_fx_order_id`.

Transfer webhooks (subscribe a `BANK_CONNECT` endpoint to `bank_transfer.*`): `bank_transfer.created`, `bank_transfer.completed`, `bank_transfer.failed`, `bank_transfer.returned`. Their `data`: `transferId`, `connectionId`, `accountId`, `bankEftCode`, `bankName`, `status`, `rail`, `amountMinor`, `currency`, `receiverIbanMasked`, `receiverNameMasked`, `paymentPurpose`, `description`, `failureCode`, `idempotencyKey`, `createdAt`, `completedAt`, `failedAt`, `returnedAt`. item.name: Sanction
item.description:
Sanctions screening (`/api/v1/sanction/*`, product `SANCTION_SERVICE`). One request per API-key route; the route table is the Node SDK's `SANCTION_ROUTES` (PHP `Sanction\SanctionRoutes`).

- **Auth:** the access token minted from your API key (`Authorization: Bearer`). The collection also signs every request; the sanction routes do not need the signature.
- **Permission:** `sanction:view_results` on the key (`403 auth.permission.forbidden` otherwise).
- **Matches, not verdicts.** An empty `matches` / `hits` is clear only when `status` is `success` and `coverageStatus` is `COMPLETE`. `PARTIAL` is clear only for the screened domains; `DEGRADED` must be run again. A replay of a screening made before list publications carries `null` publication fields.
- **When screening cannot run** (no list publication can be pinned) the answer is `503` with `status: "failure"` (`sanction.screen_name.failed`, `sanction.wallet.failed`, `sanction.transaction.failed`, `sanction.public_procurement.failed`). Hold the record as not screened and retry; never read it as "no match".
- **Ids:** the top-level `requestId` is the HTTP request's; the screening's id is `data.screeningRequestId`.
- Not here, on purpose: the screening report PDF (panel session only), adding deny-list entries, analyst decisions and case assignment (permissions an API key does not carry), list-source syncs.

Chaining: `Screen Name` stores `data.screeningRequestId` in `sanction_screening_request_id` and, when `sanction_entity_id` is empty, the first match's `entityId`; `Search Entities` fills `sanction_entity_id` when it is empty. The entity requests need `sanction_entity_id`: run one of the two first or set it yourself. The names in the bodies are fictional.

exec: // Chains the screening id and an entity id. The screening id is always replaced by the
// latest name screening; the entity id is filled only when it is empty (set it to pin one).
const sanctionPayload = sanctionEnvelope && typeof sanctionEnvelope.data === 'object' && sanctionEnvelope.data !== null
const firstMatch = Array.isArray(sanctionPayload.matches) && sanctionPayload.matches.length > 0 ? sanctionPayload.matches[0] : null;
const firstEntity = Array.isArray(sanctionPayload.items) && sanctionPayload.items.length > 0 ? sanctionPayload.items[0] : null;

request.description:
Screens a person or organization against the active list publication. Returns **matches, not verdicts**.

Body: `name` (required), `subjectType` (`person` | `organization`), `country` (ISO alpha-2), `dateOfBirth`, `identifiers` (`[{type, value}]`), `riskDomains` (`sanctions`, `pep`, `rca`, `wanted`, `regulatory`, `debarment`, `ownership`, `vessel`, `securities`; omitted = every domain), `mode` (`sanctions_only` | `sanctions_pep` | `full_risk`; with `riskDomains` their intersection), `threshold` (0–1), `customerReference`.

**Reading the result:** an empty `matches` is clear only when `status` is `success` AND `coverageStatus` is `COMPLETE`. `PARTIAL` (see `uncoveredRiskDomains`) is clear only for the screened domains; `DEGRADED` must be run again.

`data.screeningRequestId` is the screening's id (stored in `sanction_screening_request_id`); the top-level `requestId` is the HTTP request's. The first match's `entityId` fills `sanction_entity_id` when it is empty.

- `400 sanction.screening.scope_invalid`: unknown `mode` or risk domain, or an empty `mode` × `riskDomains` intersection.
- `503 sanction.screen_name.failed`: no list publication could be pinned; the screening did **not** run. Never read it as "no match".

**Permission:** `sanction:view_results`.
